raw.statement: After a loss, players in the 1600-2000 band underperform relative to their own other games (tilt).
raw.rationale: Tilt after losses should lower performance relative to after wins.

raw.statement: After 3+ consecutive losses, players in the 1200-1600 band underperform.
raw.rationale: Longer losing streaks signal tilt and emotional decision-making.

raw.statement: After 3+ consecutive wins, players in the 1600-2000 band overperform (hot hand).
raw.rationale: Hot hand or confidence; also ratings lag true skill during good form.

raw.statement: The first game of a session is worse than later games for the 1200-1600 band (warm-up).
raw.rationale: Players are cold at session start; marginals show session_index<=2 is negative.

raw.statement: Very long sessions (index 20+) reduce performance in the 1600-2000 band (fatigue).
raw.rationale: Fatigue accumulates in long sessions, though selection may offset it.

raw.statement: Returning after a long gap (>1 day) lowers performance for players rated 2000-2400.
raw.rationale: Rust after a break; marginals show the longest gap bucket is negative.

raw.statement: Playing immediately after the previous game (under 3 min) lowers performance for the <1200 band.
raw.rationale: Rapid requeueing suggests impulsive play, especially after bad outcomes.

raw.statement: After a time-forfeit previous game, players in the 1200-1600 band underperform.
raw.rationale: Time-forfeit games are frustrating and may cause time-trouble habits or tilt.

raw.statement: Players rated 1600-2000 score better with White than with Black relative to expectation.
raw.rationale: The White advantage may exceed what the Elo formula captures at club level.

raw.statement: Players rated 2400+ get a larger White advantage than their Elo expectation implies.
raw.rationale: At high level the first-move advantage and preparation matter more.

raw.statement: In 180+0 bullet-like games, the stronger player (elo_diff>100) underperforms the Elo expectation.
raw.rationale: Faster games add variance, compressing results toward 0.5 and giving favourites negative residuals.

raw.statement: In 300+3 increment games, higher-rated players outperform the Elo expectation.
raw.rationale: Increment reduces flag-driven randomness so the stronger player converts more often.

raw.statement: Tournament arena games lead to better performance than pool games for the 1600-2000 band (motivation).
raw.rationale: Arena participants are more motivated and warmed up, with berserk and streak incentives.

raw.statement: Late night UTC hours (0-5) reduce performance for the 1600-2000 band.
raw.rationale: Tiredness and alcohol in late-night play.

raw.statement: Friday-night games (UTC 19-23) show lower performance for the 1200-1600 band.
raw.rationale: Social or recreational play on Friday evenings tends to be less focused.

raw.statement: Playing against much weaker opponents (elo_diff>200) after a loss yields larger negative residuals for 1600-2000 players.
raw.rationale: Tilted players may be careless or rush against weaker opponents, and their upset losses are costly.

raw.statement: Underdogs (elo_diff<-100) in the 1200-1600 band overperform after a win streak.
raw.rationale: Rating lags a hot player's true strength, so an underdog on a streak is probably underrated.

raw.statement: Opening family A (flank openings) yields lower residuals than family B for 1600-2000 players.
raw.rationale: Marginal means show A below B; irregular openings may be less well prepared against.

raw.statement: After an abandoned previous game, players underperform in the next game.
raw.rationale: Abandoned games signal disruption such as connection issues or distraction that carries over.

raw.statement: The first game of the UTC day is worse than later games for 1600-2000 players.
raw.rationale: The marginal mean for games_played_today<=1 is -0.0083, the lowest of any bucket. This suggests a cold-start effect at the start of the day.

raw.statement: Games 1-2 of a session underperform for 1600-2000 players.
raw.rationale: Session index <=2 has a marginal mean of -0.004 against positive means later. The warm-up effect may be larger in the 1600-2000 band and extend beyond game 1.

raw.statement: Returning after more than ~110 minutes lowers performance for 1200-1600 players.
raw.rationale: The gap bucket above 110 minutes has a marginal mean of -0.004 against about +0.001 to +0.002 for shorter gaps.

raw.statement: Rating favourites (elo_diff>42) underperform the Elo expectation among 1600-2000 players.
raw.rationale: The marginal mean for elo_diff>42 is -0.0054 and for elo_diff<-42 is +0.0036. This is consistent with a compressed true-skill spread relative to Elo.

raw.statement: Underdogs (elo_diff<-42) overperform the Elo expectation among 1600-2000 players.
raw.rationale: This is the mirror image of the favourite effect. The marginal mean is positive for large negative elo_diff.

raw.statement: 1200-1600 players facing opponents rated below 1200 underperform.
raw.rationale: Opponents rated below 1200 have a marginal mean of -0.0035 for the player, which suggests low-rated opponents are underrated (e.g. provisional or improving players).

raw.statement: Mid-day-volume games (8-15 played earlier today) beat the player's baseline for 1600-2000 players.
raw.rationale: The marginal mean is +0.003 for 8-15 games today against -0.008 for the first game, so players may peak once warmed up.

raw.statement: Games 5-7 of a session show a warmed-up boost for 1200-1600 players.
raw.rationale: The session index bucket 4-7 has the highest marginal mean (+0.0033), against -0.004 for early games.

raw.statement: After a draw, 1600-2000 players overperform.
raw.rationale: Prev_result==draw has the highest marginal mean (+0.0019). A draw may signal a focused, steady state without the emotion of a win or loss.

raw.statement: E-family openings (Indian defences) produce positive residuals for 1600-2000 players.
raw.rationale: E has the highest marginal mean (+0.0025). Players who choose or face these openings may be better prepared.

raw.statement: D-family openings (closed/queen pawn) beat C-family openings for 1200-1600 players.
raw.rationale: C has the lowest marginal mean (-0.0018) among the large families and D is positive. Open tactical C games may be volatile for mid-rated players.

raw.statement: Quick-fire games after a win (<4 minutes) give 1200-1600 players a hot-hand boost.
raw.rationale: Immediate continuation after a win versus after a loss isolates momentum and tilt without gap confounding.

raw.statement: After a time-forfeit loss in the previous game, an immediate next game (<3 min) is worse for 1600-2000 players.
raw.rationale: Losing on time is frustrating, and a quick rematch may trigger tilt more than a normal loss.

raw.statement: Friday games underperform for 1600-2000 players.
raw.rationale: Friday has a marginal mean of -0.002 against about -0.0004 for other days. Tired or socially distracted players may play worse.

raw.statement: Arena tournament games lift <1200 players above their pool-game baseline.
raw.rationale: Tournament games have a higher marginal mean (+0.0001 vs -0.0009), and low-rated players may be more engaged or more competitive with points at stake.

raw.statement: After 2+ consecutive losses, <1200 players underperform.
raw.rationale: Lower-rated players may tilt more under repeated losses, and a threshold of -2 gives more power than -3.

raw.statement: 2000-2400 players with Black in 180+0 games underperform.
raw.rationale: The white advantage is larger in fast no-increment games at high levels, so black may fall short of Elo expectation more often.

raw.statement: Very long sessions (index 15+) reduce performance for 2400+ players.
raw.rationale: Top players may be fatigued or play over-pressed blitz marathons, and the marginal mean for the 2400+ band is already the most negative (-0.004).

raw.statement: After 2+ straight losses, <1200 players score above their own baseline, because their rating has dipped below their true strength.
raw.rationale: The prior round showed a significant effect opposite to the tilt prediction (+0.0036). After losses, rating understates ability, so I flip the direction.

raw.statement: D-family openings beat C-family openings for 1600-2000 players.
raw.rationale: D versus C was significant for 1200-1600 (+0.0026). Open tactical C games may be higher-variance and less favourable to the player than quieter D structures, so I test the next band up.

raw.statement: Returning after a gap of more than 10 hours lowers performance for 1200-1600 players.
raw.rationale: The >110 minute gap was nearly significant (-0.0015). A longer gap means a colder start and should give a larger effect.

raw.statement: The first game of a session is worse than the player's other games for <1200 players.
raw.rationale: The marginal first-game and short-session means are negative. Weaker players may have the least consistent warm-up.

raw.statement: 1600-2000 favourites (elo_diff>42) score above their own baseline, because Elo expectation overstates favourites' edge less than it does for typical games.
raw.rationale: The prior test of underperformance gave +0.0012 with p=0.95, so I flip the direction. Within-player demeaning may reverse the raw marginal pattern.

raw.statement: E-family openings (Indian setups) give positive residuals for 1200-1600 players relative to other games.
raw.rationale: E was positive in the marginals (+0.0025) and in the 1600-2000 test (+0.0031, p=0.08). A band with more games gives more power.

raw.statement: After a time-forfeit loss, <1200 players underperform in the next game.
raw.rationale: Losing on time is frustrating and low-rated players may be more prone to tilt. The condition does not require a short gap.

raw.statement: Friday games lower performance for 2000-2400 players.
raw.rationale: Friday has a negative marginal (-0.002), and early-UTC Friday hours could mean tired or intoxicated play. This is a different band and hours from the earlier tests.

raw.statement: Arena tournament games lift 2000-2400 players above their pool baseline.
raw.rationale: Tournament games had a positive marginal (+0.00013 vs -0.0009). Stronger players take arenas seriously and may be better prepared.

raw.statement: 1200-1600 players facing opponents rated below 1200 overperform their own baseline.
raw.rationale: The underperformance test returned +0.0019 with p=0.88, so I flip the direction. Low-rated opponents may be underrated, for example from rating deflation.

raw.statement: Games 4-7 of a session show a warmed-up boost for 1600-2000 players.
raw.rationale: The marginal for session index 4-7 is the highest (+0.0033), consistent with warm-up. The earlier 1200-1600 test was null, so I try 1600-2000.

raw.statement: Chasing a loss with an immediate next game (<2 minutes gap) hurts 1200-1600 players.
raw.rationale: Instantly re-queueing after a loss signals emotional chasing. The earlier quick-fire test followed a win and was null.

raw.statement: 2400+ players with Black in 180+0 games underperform their baseline.
raw.rationale: The 2000-2400 test was null. The White advantage is largest at the top level in fast games, so black residuals may be lower there.

raw.statement: The first game of a session is worse than the player's other games for 1600-2000 players.
raw.rationale: Games 1-2 gave -0.0008 (p=0.07). Narrowing to game 1 only should concentrate the warm-up effect.

raw.statement: Underdogs (elo_diff<-100) in the <1200 band overperform their own baseline.
raw.rationale: The lowest elo_diff bucket has a positive marginal (+0.0036), and low-rated ratings are noisy and volatile. The 1600-2000 test was null, so I try a different band and a stricter threshold.

raw.statement: After a draw, 1200-1600 players overperform their baseline.
raw.rationale: The draw marginal is the highest (+0.0019). The 1600-2000 effect was +0.0003, so I test a band with more volatile ratings.

raw.statement: Returning after a gap of more than 3 hours lowers performance for 1600-2000 players relative to their own other games.
raw.rationale: Long gaps show the weakest marginal residuals (-0.004). The ledger covers gaps for other bands, so this tests the largest band with a different threshold.

raw.statement: Friday games lower performance for players rated below 1200.
raw.rationale: Friday was significantly negative for 2000-2400 and the marginal Friday mean is the lowest of the weekdays. The effect may extend to the lowest band.

raw.statement: 2000-2400 rated favourites (elo_diff>42) score above their own baseline.
raw.rationale: The same favourite effect was marginally positive for 1600-2000 (p=0.048). Elo expectation may be miscalibrated for favourites in higher bands too.

raw.statement: After 3+ straight losses, 1600-2000 players score above their own baseline.
raw.rationale: The losing-streak rebound worked for <1200 players, because a rating dip below true strength understates their expected score. The same mechanism should apply to the largest band.

raw.statement: The first game of the UTC day is worse than later games for 1200-1600 players.
raw.rationale: Games played today <=1 have a strongly negative marginal mean (-0.008). This is a warm-up or rustiness effect, tested in a band not yet covered for this feature.

raw.statement: 300+0 games lower performance for 1600-2000 players relative to their games at other time controls.
raw.rationale: The marginal residual for 300+0 (-0.0014) is below that for 180+0 (-0.0001). Comparing against 180+0 within the same player isolates the time-control effect.

raw.statement: After a draw, players rated below 1200 overperform their baseline.
raw.rationale: Post-draw games have the highest marginal residual (+0.0019). Low-rated players are more affected by the emotional neutrality or calm of a draw, so the pooled effect may show up in this band.

raw.statement: 2000-2400 underdogs (elo_diff<-42) overperform the Elo expectation.
raw.rationale: Residuals are higher for negative elo_diff (+0.0036) and lower for positive (-0.0054), which suggests Elo expectation is too extreme. High-band players have compressed rating spreads.

raw.statement: Players rated below 1200 score better with White than with Black relative to their own baseline.
raw.rationale: Elo ignores the White first-move advantage. Low-rated players may convert it differently, so this tests a band not covered by the colour ledger entries.

raw.statement: Deep sessions (index 8+) boost performance for players rated below 1200.
raw.rationale: Marginal residuals rise with session index (+0.003 for indices above 7), consistent with selection into longer sessions. This is not covered for the lowest band.

raw.statement: C-family openings (open games) give lower residuals for 2000-2400 players than other openings.
raw.rationale: C has the lowest marginal residual among the large opening families (-0.0018). Strong players facing sharp open games may be more exposed to opponent preparation.

raw.statement: Arena tournament games lift 1200-1600 players above their pool baseline.
raw.rationale: Tournament games have a higher marginal residual (+0.0001 vs -0.0009). Arena incentives such as streak points and the time pressure of a fixed window may raise effort for mid-rated players.

raw.statement: After a time-forfeit previous game, 2000-2400 players underperform in the next game.
raw.rationale: Time-forfeit previous games have a lower marginal residual than normal endings (-0.0009 vs +0.0006). Strong players who flagged may carry time-pressure stress or rush into the next game.
